purpose: Offline static-review repair candidate: build/link/UF2 verification and host-suite evidence only. No hardware run, flashing, packaging, audio or physical-routing claim.

probe_before_after.current_result: ./tests/test_mic_recovery_integration.py --probe prints 'Ignored initial START: bounded AACP retry with uninterrupted playback passed'

deviations: CI runs Ubuntu 24.04; local Ubuntu 26.04.1 CMake 4.2.3 requires -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 for 3rd-party/ldacBT.
Host pioasm/elf2uf2 built with gcc-14/g++-14 because /usr/bin/c++ is clang 22 and breaks pinned SDK host tools.
Arm GNU Toolchain 13.2.rel1 tarball under git-ignored .tools/ approximates the Ubuntu noble package.
ccache, CI caches and the optional 32-bit codec-heap audit were not reproduced (no 32-bit multilib, no sudo).
limitations: The optional 32-bit codec-heap audit was not produced locally (no 32-bit multilib, no sudo). apply_codec_heap_audit() sets runtime_allocation_verified only after validating an audit, and packaging requires that flag for USBPods candidates, so an unaudited local build cannot be packaged.
TinyUSB timer-IRQ/main-loop serialization and UAC1 44.1 host behavior are statically argued, not host-observed.
The final review verified repairs read-only; it did not rerun the full suite or target builds. Physical routing, RF/acoustic behavior, gesture semantics and soak results remain live-only.

final_review.verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — one medium tooling defect (codec-heap gate unsatisfiable); no firmware regression, all 10 earlier findings verified fixed
final_review.disposition: Fixed in 3c9a034 (apply_codec_heap_audit validates a 32-bit audit and only then sets runtime_allocation_verified=true; unit tests cover valid plus five invalid audits). A full package() success-path integration test remains a known gap while packaging is paused.

reproducibility.fix: SUPPRESS_BUILD_DATE_INFO on the fdk-aac target; banner prints USBPODS_BUILD_SHA instead of build date/time
reproducibility.verified: two independent clean rpi0065/AAC-ELD builds in fresh build directories produced the identical UF2 sha256 c87b378ee883099d592cac89cef0ea6db072e258afbeb7af7de9d45206642972
reproducibility.caveat: hashes are tied to the embedded source SHA, so rebuilding a later docs-only commit changes the SHA field (not the firmware sources)
